summary: The article describes a surge of new small businesses in the city since September 1, 2023, and argues that shopping locally strengthens the local economy. It profiles new shops on Main Street and Elm Avenue, cites studies on local spending and job creation, and notes challenges like capital access and e-commerce competition. It also covers city and community support efforts such as the Small Business Assistance Program and the Downtown Business Alliance.
one_line: New small businesses opening since September 2023 are boosting the local economy, jobs and community identity, supported by city programs and local shoppers.
key_facts: Since September 1, 2023, the town has seen a surge in community-based small business openings.
Pam's Pantry, owned by Pamela Rodriguez, opened September 15 and sells artisanal jams and locally-sourced honey.
The Green Nook, an ecofriendly boutique founded by Kevin Tran, has been on Elm Avenue since October 3 and sells sustainable clothing and accessories.
A Local Economic Development Association (LEDA) study says about 67 cents of every dollar spent at a small business stays in the local community, versus only 40 cents at a large retail chain.
Councilwoman Linda Jeffries spoke at a community meeting on November 8, saying shopping small invests in better schools, public services and infrastructure.
Mike's Mechanics, an auto-repair shop owned by Mike Harrington, opened September 25 and offers apprenticeships to locals.
According to the Small Business Administration (SBA), small enterprises accounted for 64% of new U.S. jobs over the past two decades.
The city launched the Small Business Assistance Program (SBAP) on October 12, offering low-interest loans and grants to qualifying new businesses.
On November 22, local owners including Jennifer Reeves of the children's bookstore Once Upon A Time formed the Downtown Business Alliance (DBA).
The Emerald Thread, a handmade jewelry boutique, opened September 20, and The Tech Toolkit, offering bespoke computer repair, opened September 29.
Mayor Anita Jennings said small business contributions helped the city undertake major public projects.
A record number of citizens turned out for Small Business Saturday on November 25.
Bill's Bistro, a farm-to-table restaurant, opened October 18.
Challenges for small businesses include access to capital, rising operating costs and competition from e-commerce giants.
